title: Which Strand Does the Polymerase Read

scenes.tts: Here is a stretch of DNA, eighteen base pairs long. A cell copies part of it into RNA. Which strand does RNA polymerase read, and which way does it go? Look at the bare duplex. Nothing in it says. You need the RNA that was made, or you need a promoter.
scenes.visual: Two 18-letter strands appear; a 'template?' tag jumps between them and a '? direction' pair of arrows stays unresolved; empty RNA slots wait below.
scenes.narration: Here is a stretch of DNA, eighteen base pairs long. A cell copies part of it into RNA. Which strand does RNA polymerase read, and which way does it go? Look at the bare duplex. Nothing in it says. You need the RNA that was made, or you need a promoter.

scenes.tts: First, the rules of the reaction. RNA polymerase opens a short stretch of the helix. It uses one strand as a guide. That strand is the template strand. The enzyme lines up RNA letters by base pairing, with U opposite A. It joins each new letter to the three prime hydroxyl of the chain. So the RNA grows five prime to three prime. The RNA is antiparallel to its template. So the polymerase reads the template three prime to five prime.
scenes.visual: A short duplex opens under a polymerase blob; the guide strand turns blue, RNA letters pair beneath it, the 3' end grows leftward, and two arrows show direction.
scenes.caption: First, the rules of the reaction. RNA polymerase opens a short stretch of the helix. It uses one strand as a guide. That strand is the template strand. The enzyme lines up RNA letters by base pairing, with U opposite A. It joins each new letter to the 3′ hydroxyl of the chain. So the RNA grows 5′ to 3′. The RNA is antiparallel to its template. So the polymerase reads the template 3′ to 5′.
scenes.narration: First, the rules of the reaction. RNA polymerase opens a short stretch of the helix. It uses one strand as a guide. That strand is the template strand. The enzyme lines up RNA letters by base pairing, with U opposite A. It joins each new letter to the 3′ hydroxyl of the chain. So the RNA grows 5′ to 3′. The RNA is antiparallel to its template. So the polymerase reads the template 3′ to 5′.

scenes.tts: Now use the real RNA. It reads A, C, G, U, U, U, C, A, U, G, G. The RNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with U in place of T. So look for that sequence, reading five prime to three prime. Read the bottom strand from right to left. It spells A, C, G, T, T, T, C, A, T, G, G. That matches. The top strand does not contain it. So the bottom strand is the coding strand.
scenes.visual: The RNA string appears; letters of the bottom strand are read right to left into a readout row that lines up with the RNA; U versus T flash; bottom strand turns yellow.
scenes.caption: Now use the real RNA. It reads A, C, G, U, U, U, C, A, U, G, G. The RNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with U in place of T. So look for that sequence, reading 5′ to 3′. Read the bottom strand from right to left. It spells A, C, G, T, T, T, C, A, T, G, G. That matches. The top strand does not contain it. So the bottom strand is the coding strand.
scenes.narration: Now use the real RNA. It reads A, C, G, U, U, U, C, A, U, G, G. The RNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with U in place of T. So look for that sequence, reading 5′ to 3′. Read the bottom strand from right to left. It spells A, C, G, T, T, T, C, A, T, G, G. That matches. The top strand does not contain it. So the bottom strand is the coding strand.

scenes.tts: The template is the other strand, the top one. Check it by pairing. The RNA lies antiparallel to the top strand. The first RNA letter, A, pairs with the top strand's T, at the right end. C pairs with G, G with C, and so on leftward. Every letter pairs. The top strand is the template.
scenes.visual: The coding strand lifts away, the RNA settles above the top strand letter by letter from the right, ticks show each pair, and the top strand turns blue.
scenes.narration: The template is the other strand, the top one. Check it by pairing. The RNA lies antiparallel to the top strand. The first RNA letter, A, pairs with the top strand's T, at the right end. C pairs with G, G with C, and so on leftward. Every letter pairs. The top strand is the template.

scenes.tts: Now watch the enzyme work. The polymerase reads the template three prime to five prime. On the top strand, three prime is at the right. So the polymerase moves right to left along the page. The RNA grows five prime to three prime in that same leftward direction. Its five prime end lies toward the right of the duplex.
scenes.visual: The RNA clears; a polymerase blob enters at the right end and slides left, adding one RNA letter at a time; the 5' end stays right, the growing 3' end moves left.
scenes.caption: Now watch the enzyme work. The polymerase reads the template 3′ to 5′. On the top strand, 3′ is at the right. So the polymerase moves right to left along the page. The RNA grows 5′ to 3′ in that same leftward direction. Its 5′ end lies toward the right of the duplex.

scenes.tts: Two checks catch most mistakes. The RNA must be antiparallel to its template. And a bare duplex, with no RNA and no promoter, does not tell you which strand is the template. So find the RNA. Keep this rule: the RNA matches the coding strand and pairs with the template.
scenes.visual: The coloured picture gets two opposite arrows; then the colours drain to a bare duplex with question marks; the RNA returns and the colours come back; the rule appears.
